code_actions.rationale: No imaging or consultant documentation of nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage; CT and consults describe basal-ganglia ICH with IVH and obstructive hydrocephalus instead (CT impression p.287).

No explicit provider diagnosis of 'cerebral edema' found in the retrieved documentation; notes and imaging describe obstructive hydrocephalus and hematoma/mass effect rather than a discrete documented diagnosis of cerebral edema (CT impression p.287; Discharge summary p.909).

Obstructive hydrocephalus is documented by CT and neurosurgical evaluation with emergent EVD placement and later VP shunt; per policy this meets MCC criteria (Neurosurgery consult p.261; EVD procedure p.392; VP shunt procedure p.856). Severity changed to MCC.

The chart specifically documents 'cerebral salt wasting' and discharge states 'cerebral salt wasting resolved'; SIADH is not explicitly established in provider documentation nor fully supported by the required SIADH workup. Remove E22.2 and code hyponatremia instead.
Right hemiplegia was present on arrival (H&P shows dense right hemiplegia), so POA should be Y.
Speech impairment (inability to speak) was documented on arrival; update POA to Y.
Record documents a VP shunt placement and subsequent shunt-dependent communicating hydrocephalus; there is no documentation of an intracranial neurostimulator. Z98.62 is unsupported.
Provider documents 'cerebral salt wasting with hypotonic hyponatremia' and resolution during the stay; add hyponatremia (E87.1) rather than SIADH (Discharge summary p.909; H&P p.322).

evidence.quote: Emergent CT head demonstrated a large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus.
Large left basal-ganglia hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH and early obstructive hydrocephalus.
Indication for Procedure: Obstructive hydrocephalus with ICH/IVH
ABG (02:00): pH 7.30 / PaCO2 47 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 17; lactate 5.1 mmol/L; P/F ratio 73.
hospital-acquired Klebsiella pneumoniae ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefepime
Cerebral salt wasting with hypotonic hyponatremia
ventriculoperitoneal shunt-dependent communicating hydrocephalus; tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status (weaning to trach collar); resolved Klebsiella VAP; cerebral salt wasting resolved;
Under general anesthesia, right frontal ventricular catheter placed. Programmable valve tunneled subcutaneously to peritoneal cavity via mini-laparotomy. Distal catheter placed intraperitoneally.
Chief Complaint: "Sudden severe headache, then he couldn't move his right side or speak."
Ventilation via tracheostomy with progressive weaning trials;
CSF characteristics Bloody CSF returned; ICP 24 initially
On arrival GCS had declined to 6 with impaired airway protection.
Admit: Neurocritical Care Unit. Condition: critical. Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2, ICP; strict SBP target < 140.

system_note: Audit of MR_11 (entire inpatient stay): Principal diagnosis I61.0 (left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH) is supported by the admitting H&P and radiology (CT) (History & Physical (Admitting), p.322; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Head Without Contrast, p.287). External ventricular drain (EVD) and later ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement are documented and support hydrocephalus coding and related neurosurgical management (Procedure Note - Emergent External Ventricular Drain Placement, p.392; Procedure Note - Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Placement, p.856). The record documents emergent intubation and objective hypoxemia (ABG/P/F) meeting the validation criteria for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ED Provider Note, p.322; Neurosurgery Consultation, p.261). Klebsiella ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) treated with cefepime is documented in the hospital course and supports organism/attribution coding (Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.909). Documented, supported items (representative citations): - ICH with IVH and obstructive hydrocephalus (History & Physical, p.322; CT Head impression, p.287) (ev_0001, ev_0002). These support I61.0 as principal and G91.1 as a concurrent neurosurgical condition with CSF diversion procedures (ev_0003, ev_0008). - Emergent intubation and mechanical ventilation with objective hypoxemia (ED/critical care notes and ABG with PaO2 66, P/F 73) support J96.01 as acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (ev_0004). Respiratory therapy and prolonged ventilator course/tracheostomy support the prolonged ventilation code (ev_0010, ev_0007). - Klebsiella VAP and treatment with cefepime documented in the discharge summary supports coding of pneumonia and organism (J15.9 and B96.1) (ev_0005). Errors/unsupported items found and rationale for correction (with citations): 1) G91.1 (Obstructive hydrocephalus) was billed as CC but the governing policy and the clinical documentation (CT showing IVH obstructing CSF flow; emergent EVD placement; later VP shunt) meet criteria for the MCC designation. Change severity to MCC (Neurosurgery Consultation, p.261; EVD procedure note, p.392; VP shunt procedure, p.856) (ev_0003, ev_0008). 2) I97.5 (nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage) is not supported by the imaging or consults. CT and radiologist impression document large left basal-ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with IVH and obstructive hydrocephalus; no subdural is described. Remove I97.5 (CT Head impression, p.287) (ev_0002). 3) G93.6 (cerebral edema) is not explicitly documented as a provider diagnosis in the retrieved clinical notes; imaging and neurosurgical documentation instead describe obstructive hydrocephalus from IVH and mass effect. Remove G93.6 (CT Head impression and Discharge/Transfer Summary show hydrocephalus/IVH/hematoma rather than a discrete, documented diagnosis of 'cerebral edema') (ev_0002, ev_0007). 4) E22.2 (SIADH) was billed but the chart documents 'cerebral salt wasting' as the hyponatremia mechanism. The SIADH validation criteria require either explicit provider diagnosis of SIADH or specific laboratory workup / exclusions; here the provider documented cerebral salt wasting and discharge notes state it resolved. Remove E22.2 and instead add an appropriate hyponatremia code (E87.1) to reflect the documented hypotonic hyponatremia/cerebral salt wasting (History & Physical, p.322; Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.909) (ev_0006, ev_0007). 5) G81.94 (hemiplegia, right) and R47.1 (dysarthria) are documented on arrival (H&P: dense right hemiplegia; chief complaint inability to speak). Both were billed with POA=N; documentation shows these were present on admission. Update POA to Y for these codes (History & Physical, p.322) (ev_0009). 6) Z98.62 (presence of intracranial neurostimulator) is unsupported in the record. The record documents a VP shunt (ventriculoperitoneal shunt) but does not document an intracranial neurostimulator. Remove Z98.62 (Procedure Note - Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Placement, p.856; Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.909) (ev_0008, ev_0007). 7) Tracheostomy approach (percutaneous vs open) is ambiguous in the retrieved documentation: the H&P references a percutaneous tracheostomy but the billed PCS is an open bypass code. This conflict must be resolved before confirming the exact ICD-10-PCS tracheostomy code. Human review needed (see HITL question below). Summary correction actions applied to the claim (below in code_decisions and revised lists). Key supporting citations: History & Physical (Admitting), p.322 (ev_0001/ev_0012//ev_0009); Diagnostic Imaging CT Head, p.287 (ev_0002); Procedure Note - Emergent EVD Placement, p.392 (ev_0003); Neurosurgery Consultation, p.261 (/ev_0004); Procedure Note - VP Shunt, p.856 (ev_0008); Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.909 (ev_0007); ED Provider Note, p.322 ; Respiratory Therapy Note, p.131 (ev_0010).
rationale_letter: Date: 2026-10-15 To: Medical Records / Coding Department Re: MR_11 - Audit Determination (Complete DRG review) We performed a DRG-level audit of the inpatient stay for Mei-Lin Zhang (admit 04/26/2026-transfer 08/29/2026). We reviewed the billed diagnosis and procedure set against the medical record and the applicable condition validation guidance. The medical record supports the principal diagnosis of intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension and obstructive hydrocephalus, associated neurosurgical procedures, mechanical ventilation, and a ventilator-associated Klebsiella pneumonia. However, several coding inaccuracies were identified that require correction. Finding (summary): 1) Severity misclassification: G91.1 (obstructive hydrocephalus) was billed at CC but meets MCC criteria because imaging and neurosurgical documentation show obstructive hydrocephalus from IVH with CSF diversion (EVD and subsequent VP shunt) (Neurosurgery Consultation 04/26/2026; EVD procedure note 04/26/2026; VP shunt procedure 05/13/2026). This should be coded as MCC. 2) Unsupported/incorrect diagnoses removed: I97.5 (subdural hemorrhage) and G93.6 (cerebral edema) do not appear in the diagnostic imaging or consultant impressions and are not supported as active diagnoses in the chart; these should be removed. Z98.62 (intracranial neurostimulator) is unsupported and should be removed. 3) SIADH (E22.2) is not supported - the record documents cerebral salt wasting and hyponatremia rather than provider-confirmed SIADH; remove E22.2 and report hyponatremia (E87.1) consistent with the documentation. 4) POA flag corrections: G81.94 (right hemiplegia) and R47.1 (speech disturbance) are documented on arrival and should be POA=Y rather than POA=N. 5) Tracheostomy PCS approach unclear: the chart contains conflicting indications about whether the tracheostomy was percutaneous vs open. Human clarification is required to confirm the correct PCS code for the tracheostomy technique. Correction being made: The claim's diagnosis list will retain I61.0 as principal; remove unsupported codes I97.5, G93.6, E22.2, Z98.62; add E87.1 (hyponatremia) to reflect documented cerebral salt wasting; change G91.1 to MCC; change POA flags for hemiplegia and dysarthria to Y. The procedure list retains documented EVD, VP shunt, endotracheal intubation, PEG, arterial line, central line, prolonged mechanical ventilation; tracheostomy coding will be held pending clarification of approach. Representative supporting documentation: History & Physical (04/26/2026) and CT Head (04/26/2026) documenting left basal-ganglia ICH with IVH and obstructive hydrocephalus, emergent EVD placement (04/26/2026), VP shunt placement (05/13/2026), emergent intubation, ABG showing PaO2 66/P/F 73 on admission, and discharge summary describing Klebsiella VAP treated with cefepime. If you disagree with the above corrections or can provide definitive documentation resolving the tracheostomy technique (percutaneous vs open), please provide the operative/procedure note or signed documentation specifying the approach so we may finalize the PCS code. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
